item.title: Rep. Himes: Iran Regime Not ‘On the Verge of Collapse’
item.description: Rep. Jim Himes, the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, says he does not believe Iran's regime is on the verge of collapse and warns that additional economic pressure could produce "blowback" on American consumers through higher energy and goods prices. Himes also criticizes Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's leadership of the Pentagon amid fresh scrutiny following Army Secretary Dan Driscoll's resignation. And ahead of the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, Himes says the US is safer today, but must remain flexible and prepared for emerging national security threats. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s New Birthright Citizenship Curbs Halted by Court for Now
item.description: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration from carrying out for now the president’s latest effort to impose new limits on automatic birthright citizenship after losing an earlier legal fight before the US Supreme Court.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

item.title: California’s Would-Be Next Governor Takes on Trump Over Voters
item.description: A California immigrant-rights group supported by the state’s Democratic candidate for governor, Xavier Becerra, sued the Trump administration for allegedly trying to suppress the voting rights of non-US born citizens by imposing a new federal list of eligible voters.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson

item.title: Rodríguez Vows Elections Will Happen When Venezuela ‘Is Ready’
item.description: Venezuela’s Delcy Rodríguez assured citizens that a presidential election would “without a doubt” take place when the country “is ready,” but refrained from sharing a timeline.
item.dc:creator: Fabiola Zerpa

item.title: UK and France Plan to Counter People-Smugglers’ ‘Mega-Dinghies’
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham will discuss efforts to stop so-called mega-dinghies carrying hundreds of migrants across the English Channel when he meets his French counterpart Emmanuel Macron on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Lucy White

item.title: Brazil Passes Critical Minerals Bill Tightening Deal Scrutiny
item.description: Brazil’s Congress approved a critical minerals bill that gives the government greater scrutiny over mining deals, despite warnings from the industry that the rules risk deterring foreign investment.
item.dc:creator: Mariana Durao and Daniel Carvalho

item.title: What to Expect When Republicans Meet Next Week in Dallas
item.description: Josh Wingrove, Bloomberg senior White House reporter, breaks down what to expect next week when Republicans come to Dallas for their first-ever midterm convention. Speaking with Bloomberg's Julie Fine, he also looks ahead to the major Senate races that could change the balance of power in Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed Sees Modest Wage Growth, Dell Gets Boost | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 9/2/2026
item.description: The August Beige Book drops and shows both wages and prices are up moderately across the country. Bloomberg TV & Radio Economics & Policy Correspondent Mike McKee reacts. Then, Bloomberg News Washington Correspondent Tyler Kendall sits down the with the CEO of Chevron to discuss the Venezuela oil partnership. Plus, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Analyst Woo Jin Ho talks market reaction to Dell's boosted sales outlook. With autonomous driving becoming more popularized in our vehicles, car insurance companies are finding new ways to price insurance. Lemonade CEO Daniel Schreiber explains how his insurance company is evolving alongside the auto industry. Finally, 'Our Town' Podcast Co-Hosts Meribah Knight and Susan Berfield talk about the small Tennessee town at the heart of a fight over Christian Nationalism. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Surging Bond Yields Aren’t Deterring US Lawmakers From More Debt
item.description: The latest comments from the Capitol give bond investors even more reason to be skeptical.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson

item.title: Trump to Levy More Chip Tariffs | Radio Balance of Power: Early Edition 9/2/2026
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Kailey Leinz discusses the latest from DC. On today's show, Republican Congressman Jodey Arrington of Texas, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Estonian Defense Minister Resigns Over Munitions Scandal
item.description: Estonian Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur resigned from government following a furor over a botched European Union-funded deal to buy artillery shells for Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Ott Tammik

item.title: Trump Says He’s ‘Happy’ Prince Harry, Meghan Markle Leaving US
item.description: President Donald Trump celebrated Prince Harry and his wife Meghan Markle’s plans to leave the US, taking a dig at the royal couple as they return to live in the UK.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan

item.title: Trump Says Iran Strikes to Be Short, Asserts Hormuz Control
item.description: President Donald Trump said renewed attacks on Iran would likely be short-lived, reiterating his claim that the US controls the crucial Strait of Hormuz after fresh fighting spiked energy prices and rekindled fears of an open-ended war.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse and Patrick Sykes

item.title: Bessent Blames High Energy Prices on Ukraine’s Russia Strikes
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian energy facilities were one reason for rising global energy prices, citing those attacks before mentioning the war against Iran when asked about the elevated cost of living in the US.
item.dc:creator: Yash Roy

item.title: Commerce Secretary Lutnick on AI, Anthropic and Canada Talks
item.description: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick lauds the benefits of artificial intelligence. Speaking with Joe Mathieu at the G20 Innovation Ministerial in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, Lutnick also says Anthropic has settled differences with the Trump administration and discusses the state of US-Canada trade negotiations. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Hails US Summer Travel Bump After Second-Term Doldrums
item.description: President Donald Trump claimed credit for a spike in summer travel during a meeting with airline, hotel and cruise industry executives, as he seeks to regain political momentum at a pivotal moment.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse

item.title: Carney Extends Gas Tax Break as War Keeps Energy Costs High
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government will extend the suspension of a fuel excise tax to Jan. 31, 2027, a move that comes amid surging energy costs fueled by the war in Iran.
item.dc:creator: Brian Platt and Mathieu Dion

item.title: Brazil Presidential Election Tightens as Bolsonaro Seizes Momentum From Lula
item.description: Brazil’s presidential race has become a toss-up a month before the election, with leftist leader Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s advantage fading thanks to a slowing economy and fallout from corruption allegations against his son.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Diniz Tavares and Daniel Carvalho

item.title: Nepal Urges Tourists Not to Abandon Himalayas After Floods
item.description: Nepal urged international travelers not to abandon the Himalayas, declaring the country open for tourism as it continues to assess the human and economic toll from catastrophic floods that killed more than a thousand people.
item.dc:creator: Swati Pandey
